How air-conditioning made America and how it could break us all

Let's talk about how to cool your home without A/C.

  1. An attic fan does wonders. They cost about $100 bucks and keeps the house ventilated. It has made my house A/C free for a whole extra month now. Before the attic fan we started using A/C in late May and used it until mid to late September. (We live in the South). After using the attic fan, we do not start to use the A/C until late June or early July and take it out in late August.

  2. Painting or tiling your roof a lighter color helps. It can reduce temperatures inside by as much as 20% according to the manufacturer's claims. We are painting our roof reflective colors to reduce heat inside. Painting the roof white is said to help even more. We are painting our roof this year and will know just how much it actually helps next year.

  3. Adding plants to the outside of a building which climb. Plants respire which moves air around the building. Plants also have leaves that keep the hot sun off of the side of the building reducing the amount of energy it absorbs. Using just trellis and ivy or honeysuckle could reduce the temp inside a building by couple degrees.

  4. Replace old single pane windows with double pane double hung windows. Opening the windows at the top at night will help to let out the heat.

  5. Add reflective window tint to windows, an awning over windows, and use light blocking curtains which are insulated. Tint on windows can help reflect the sun's hot rays. Awnings are helpful in shading part of the window from the hottest rays of the sun. They used to be quite common all around homes in the early 50's. There are light and sound blocking curtains on the market which are insulated enough to keep some heat out of the main living space. Expect to pay for the privilege.

  6. Plants trees around your immediate area of the home. Trees help to reduce the heat around the home by blocking the sun's hot rays. Even if they do not directly shade the house, they can reduce the air temperatures around the home, which reduces passive transfer of temperature.

  7. Paint the outside of your home a light color. While this may seem like common sense, you would be surprised how many dark trailers are in the south. A lighter color home reflects more of the sun's energy.

Ten percent had to be written off per year because of "spoilage" by rats that crept in at night and nibbled on the hundred dollar bills.

The Colombian cartels' continuing struggles to maintain supremacy resulted in Colombia quickly becoming the world's murder capital with 25,100 violent deaths in 1991 and 27,100 in 1992.
